items.title: A finite initial segment of the naturals has its index as cardinality
items.statement: For each $n\in\mathbb N$, let $I_n=\{t\in\mathbb N:t<n\}$. Then $I_n=n$, so $I_n$ is finite and $|I_n|=n$.
items.strategy: Identify the additive-order initial segment with the von Neumann natural n, then use the finite-cardinality definition.

items.title: Finite partially observable Markov decision process
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite nonempty set of hidden states, $A$ a finite nonempty action set available in every state, and $\Omega$ a finite nonempty observation set. Give these sets their power-set sigma-algebras. A finite POMDP with known model consists of a finite reward alphabet $\mathcal R\subseteq\mathbb R$ and a joint probability mass $p(s',\rho\mid s,a)$ on $S\times\mathcal R$ for each $(s,a)\in S\times A$, an observation probability distribution $O(\cdot\mid s')$ on $\Omega$ for each $s'\in S$, and an initial belief $b_0:S\to[0,1]$ with $\sum_{s\in S}b_0(s)=1$. Put

$$T(s'\mid s,a)=\sum_{\rho\in\mathcal R}p(s',\rho\mid s,a),\qquad r(s,a)=\sum_{s'\in S}\sum_{\rho\in\mathcal R}\rho\,p(s',\rho\mid s,a).$$

At decision time $t$, write $S_t\in S$ for the hidden state, $A_t\in A$ for the chosen action, $R_t\in\mathcal R$ for the realized reward, and $O_{t+1}\in\Omega$ for the next observation. Conditional on $S_t=s$ and $A_t=a$, the joint law of next state $S_{t+1}=s'$, reward $R_t=\rho$, and observation $O_{t+1}=o$ is $p(s',\rho\mid s,a)O(o\mid s')$. Thus the observation depends only on the next state and is not an additional observation of the reward. A policy uses only the past actions and observations; realized rewards are not included in its history. For a horizon $H\in\mathbb N$ and discount $\gamma\in[0,1]$, the objective is to maximize $\mathbb E[\sum_{t=0}^{H-1}\gamma^tR_t]$. The model is known; learning its transition, reward, or observation laws is outside this definition.
items.strategy: Specify a finite hidden-state MDP, an action-independent next-state observation kernel, the initial belief, observed history, and a finite-horizon objective.

references.title: Kaelbling, Littman, and Cassandra, Planning and Acting in Partially Observable Stochastic Domains, Brown Technical Report CS-96-08
Russ Tedrake, Planning Under Uncertainty: Partially-observable Markov decision processes, MIT Underactuated Robotics course notes
Pascal Poupart, CS 886 Lecture 13: POMDPs, University of Waterloo

items.title: Belief states and the finite Bayes filter
items.statement:
For a finite POMDP with state set $S$, define its **belief simplex** by $\Delta(S)=\{b:S\to[0,1]:\sum_{s\in S}b(s)=1\}$, with the Euclidean subspace topology and its Borel sigma-algebra. At time $t$, the observed-history random variable is $H_t=(A_0,O_1,\ldots,A_{t-1},O_t)$, and a realized history is $h_t=(a_0,o_1,\ldots,a_{t-1},o_t)$; at $t=0$ both histories are empty. A (possibly randomized) **history policy** assigns to each finite history $h_t$ a probability distribution $\pi_t(\cdot\mid h_t)$ on $A$; a deterministic choice is the point-mass case. Let $\Pr_\pi$ be the induced finite law: multiply the initial belief, these action probabilities, and the one-step factors $p(s',\rho\mid s,a)O(o\mid s')$, and sum out hidden states and unobserved rewards when taking marginals. Thus policy randomization depends only on the observed history and is conditionally independent of the hidden state given that history. The history $h_t$ is **reachable** when $\Pr_\pi(H_t=h_t)>0$. Its **belief state** is

$$b_t(s)=\Pr_\pi(S_t=s\mid H_t=h_t)=\frac{\Pr_\pi(S_t=s,H_t=h_t)}{\Pr_\pi(H_t=h_t)},$$

where both probabilities are finite sums of products of the specified initial, action, transition, joint reward-transition, and observation probabilities, with unobserved rewards summed out. At $t=0$, the empty history has belief $b_0$.

For $b\in\Delta(S)$ and $a\in A$, define the predicted state distribution $\bar b_{b,a}(s')=\sum_{s\in S}T(s'\mid s,a)b(s)$ and, for $o\in\Omega$, the observation probability

$$q(o\mid b,a)=\sum_{s'\in S}O(o\mid s')\bar b_{b,a}(s').$$

When $q(o\mid b,a)>0$, the **Bayes filter** is the probability vector

$$\tau(b,a,o)(s')=\frac{O(o\mid s')\bar b_{b,a}(s')}{q(o\mid b,a)}.$$

When $q(o\mid b,a)=0$, $\tau(b,a,o)$ is undefined; no quotient or filler value is assigned. For each $(b,a)$, the **belief-state transition kernel** on Borel sets $C\subseteq\Delta(S)$ is

$$K(C\mid b,a)=\sum_{o\in\Omega:q(o\mid b,a)>0}q(o\mid b,a)\,1_C(\tau(b,a,o)),$$

and the expected one-step reward at belief $b$ under action $a$ is $\bar r(b,a)=\sum_{s\in S}b(s)r(s,a)$, where $1_C$ denotes the indicator function of $C$.
items.strategy: Define the finite conditional belief by its positive-history ratio, then state the normalizer, positive-probability Bayes update, and belief-state transition kernel.

items.title: Exhaustive finite-horizon POMDP alpha-vector backup
items.statement: Input a finite POMDP, a horizon H∈N, and γ∈[0,1]. Let Γ₀={0}. For h=0,…,H−1, form Γₕ₊₁ from every action a∈A and every tuple (αₒ)ₒ∈O∈Γₕ^O by adding the vector αₐ,(αₒ)(s)=r(s,a)+γΣₛ′T(s′|s,a)ΣₒO(o|s′)αₒ(s′), and remove duplicate vectors. Return Γ₀,…,Γ_H. Each α vector is indexed by S and records the conditional value of one finite observation-contingent policy tree from each possible starting state. This exhaustive procedure does not perform linear-program witness pruning and makes no bit-complexity or polynomial-time claim.
items.strategy: Enumerate all finite observation-contingent policy trees by root action and one continuation tree per observation, and compute their state-conditional values recursively.

references.title: Kaelbling, Littman, and Cassandra, Planning and Acting in Partially Observable Stochastic Domains, Brown Technical Report CS-96-08
Pascal Poupart, CS 886 Lecture 13: POMDPs, University of Waterloo

items.title: The finite POMDP Bayes filter is a probability kernel
items.statement: For every finite POMDP, belief b∈Δ(S), and action a∈A, the observation probabilities q(o|b,a) are nonnegative and sum to one. For q(o|b,a)>0, τ(b,a,o) belongs to Δ(S) and is the conditional law of the next hidden state given that observation. The map K(·|b,a) defined in the belief-state definition is a probability measure on Δ(S), and its event evaluations are Borel measurable in b, so K is a probability kernel from Δ(S)×A to Δ(S).
items.strategy: Normalize the predicted-state law and observation kernel, specialize dominated-kernel Bayes to counting measure, and prove measurability of the finite belief transition.

references.title: Kaelbling, Littman, and Cassandra, Planning and Acting in Partially Observable Stochastic Domains, Brown Technical Report CS-96-08

items.title: The belief state is a sufficient statistic for finite POMDP control
items.statement: In a finite POMDP with a known model, for every positive-probability action-observation history hₜ and selected action a, the conditional law of (Sₜ₊₁,Oₜ₊₁) given hₜ and a is determined by the current belief bₜ and a. It is Σₛbₜ(s)T(s′|s,a)O(o|s′), the observation marginal is q(o|bₜ,a), and, for positive q, the next belief is τ(bₜ,a,o). The conditional expected reward is r̄(bₜ,a). Consequently the belief process is a fully observed MDP with transition kernel K and reward r̄, and every finite-horizon optimal value depends on the history only through its belief; zero-probability observations require no update convention.
items.strategy: Factor the next-state/observation law through the current conditional state distribution, then induct on the remaining finite horizon using the finite action maximum.

items.title: Finite-horizon POMDP values are piecewise-linear and convex
items.statement: For a finite POMDP with finite nonempty S, A, and O, horizon H∈N, and γ∈[0,1], let Γₕ be the alpha-vector set returned by the exhaustive backup at horizon h. The optimal expected h-step reward from belief b is Vₕ(b)=max_{α∈Γₕ}Σₛb(s)α(s). Hence Vₕ is the upper envelope of finitely many linear functions on Δ(S), is piecewise-linear and convex, and has an attained maximum at every belief. A vector with no belief at which it attains this maximum may be removed without changing Vₕ. The number Nₕ of deterministic depth-h policy trees satisfies N₀=1 and Nₕ₊₁=|A|Nₕ^{|O|}; thus the exhaustive candidate and witness searches have finite but potentially exponentially growing tree counts. These are finite-horizon statements only; they assert no infinite-horizon representation, learning guarantee, or efficient pruning bound.
items.strategy: Induct on horizon to identify each policy tree's state-value vector, average under the initial belief, take the finite maximum, and prove envelope convexity and witness-pruning invariance.

references.title: Kaelbling, Littman, and Cassandra, Planning and Acting in Partially Observable Stochastic Domains, Brown Technical Report CS-96-08

items.title: A two-state POMDP update changes a three-to-one prior to nine-to-one
items.statement: Let S={0,1}, A={a}, O={x,y}, let the hidden state remain fixed under a, and let the reward be zero. Put b(0)=3/4 and b(1)=1/4, with O(x|0)=3/4, O(x|1)=1/4, O(y|0)=1/4, and O(y|1)=3/4. The probability of observing x is 5/8, and after x the belief is b′(0)=9/10 and b′(1)=1/10.
items.strategy: Compute the predictive observation mass and apply the finite Bayes formula coordinate by coordinate.

items.title: An observation with identical state likelihoods leaves the belief unchanged
items.statement: Let S={0,1}, A={a}, O={x}, let the hidden state remain fixed under a, and let the reward be zero. If b(0)=2/3, b(1)=1/3, and O(x|0)=O(x|1)=1, then q(x|b,a)=1 and the posterior after x is again (2/3,1/3); this observation does not distinguish the two hidden states.
items.strategy: Evaluate the common observation likelihood in the numerator and normalizer, then simplify both posterior coordinates.

items.title: A zero-likelihood observation has no posterior update
items.statement: Let S={0,1}, A={a}, O={x,y}, let the hidden state remain fixed under a, and let the reward be zero. If b(0)=1, b(1)=0, O(x|0)=1, O(y|0)=0, O(x|1)=0, and O(y|1)=1, then q(y|b,a)=0 and q(x|b,a)=1. The filter τ(b,a,y) is undefined, and the belief transition uses only the positive-mass x branch.
items.strategy: Compute the observation masses and apply the filter's stated positive-normalizer domain.

items.title: A finite POMDP family has exponentially many witnessed alpha vectors
items.statement: For each $n\in\mathbb N$ with $0<n$, let $I_n=\{t\in\mathbb N:t<n\}$ be a clock set and let a hidden binary string be a function $x:I_n\to\{0,1\}$. Write $\sigma(t)$ for the natural successor. Put $S=\{(x,t):x\in\{0,1\}^{I_n},\ t\in I_n\}$, $A=\{0,1\}$, $\Omega=\{o\}$, and reward alphabet $\mathcal R=\{0,1\}$. For $t\in I_n$, define $t^+=\sigma(t)$ if $\sigma(t)\in I_n$, and $t^+=t$ otherwise. Under action $a$ at $(x,t)$, the joint next-state/reward law assigns probability one to next state $(x,t^+)$ and reward $1_{\{a=x(t)\}}$; the sole observation $o$ occurs with probability one. Let $x^\circ:I_n\to\{0,1\}$ be the constant-zero string, take $b_0=\delta_{(x^\circ,0)}$, and set horizon $H=n$ and $\gamma=1$. There are exactly $2^n$ depth-$n$ policy trees, one for each binary action string $y:I_n\to\{0,1\}$. The alpha vector of tree $y$, evaluated at state $(x,0)$, is $\sum_{t\in I_n}1_{\{x(t)=y(t)\}}$. At the point-mass belief $\delta_{(y,0)}$ this vector has value $n$, while every distinct action string has value strictly less than $n$. Therefore all $2^n$ alpha vectors are distinct and each has a witness belief in $\Delta(S)$, which need not be reachable from the specified initial belief; the family has state count $n2^n$.
items.strategy: Count the binary action sequences, compute each deterministic tree's reward vector along the clocked state path, and use the point-mass belief at its matching string to witness unique optimality.
